column3: The Hebrew ends the genealogy with “son of a Benjamite man”; BSB compresses this to “of Benjamin.”
The Hebrew describes his height as “from his shoulder and upward” above the people; BSB renders this as “a head taller.”
The Hebrew specifically names female donkeys and has no separate introductory “One day.” It also includes a request particle and a separate command to rise, left implicit in BSB.
The Hebrew leaves Saul unnamed and repeats the verb for passing through four times. BSB supplies Saul and the servant and varies the wording of the journey.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies “the servant.” It refers to “our way on which we have gone”; BSB instead says “which way to go.”
The Hebrew explicitly says Saul spoke “to his servant.” It describes the containers as “our vessels”; BSB uses “our packs.”
The Hebrew explicitly names Saul as the recipient of the answer; BSB uses “him.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says “your word is good”; BSB retains only “Good.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew repeats “today” when explaining both his arrival and the sacrifice; BSB states it only for his arrival.
The Hebrew’s final assurance of finding him again includes an expression referring to today; BSB leaves this time reference implicit.
The Hebrew leaves the travelers unnamed; BSB identifies them as Saul and his servant.
The Hebrew uses the image of the LORD uncovering Samuel’s ear; BSB renders it as revealing something to Samuel.
The Hebrew repeats “My people” as those he will save; BSB substitutes “them.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew joins sending Saul away and telling him what is in his heart as separate statements. BSB makes the sending a “when” clause introducing the telling.
The Hebrew says not to “set your heart” on the donkeys; BSB renders this bodily expression as “do not worry about them.”
The Hebrew describes Benjamin as among the small tribes, using a plural expression; BSB calls it “the smallest tribe.”
The Hebrew says Samuel gave them a place “at the head” of the invited guests; BSB renders this as “the place of honor.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker of the instructions unnamed; BSB explicitly identifies him as Samuel.
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed and says simply “on the roof”; BSB supplies Samuel and expands the location to “the roof of his house.”
The Hebrew places the call at the rising of dawn; BSB says “just before dawn.” The command literally says “rise,” rendered “Get ready” in BSB.
The Hebrew reports the servant’s departure before the command for Saul to stand; BSB moves it to the end. It says Samuel will “cause you to hear” God’s word, rendered “reveal to you” in BSB.
